requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.

An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request. OpenAI MUST use its configured endpoint or
`https://api.openai.com/v1`, and MUST resolve `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither
`api_key` nor `api_key_env` is supplied.
rationale:
I judge that the reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`. I did not request implementation source, because each obligation maps to a test whose assertions I could read directly.

- **`--config` selection.** `an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` runs the CLI with `--config alternate`, where the workspace default points at a different, wrong configuration. It asserts that the request used `alternate-model` and that usage records it. `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` in `tests/configuration.rs` covers explicit selection at the resolver level.
- **Precedence order.** `workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections` in `tests/configuration.rs` checks each step. With both defaults present, the workspace default wins. A user project selection beats the workspace default. A workspace default that names a user configuration resolves to the user file. With no workspace default, the user default is used. `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` checks that a non-canonical root (`root.join(".")`) resolves to the canonical `project_root`. `unknown_selections_name_the_file_that_made_them` checks that a project selection outranks the default.
- **Workspace overrides same-named user configuration as a complete record, with no field merging.** The `shared` configuration appears in both files in `workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections`. The result takes the workspace `config_path`, the workspace backend and options, no endpoint, and `concurrency` of `None`. The user's region, concurrency and `top_p` do not leak through. `workspace_configurations_accept_validate_and_override_concurrency` repeats this across all three backends, with and without a workspace `concurrency`.
- **Workspace-only without a user file.** It is covered at the resolver level, with `None` as the user configuration. It is also covered end to end in `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file`, which deletes the user file. That test asserts the workspace model is used, the workspace file is unchanged, and no user file is created.
- **Missing configuration or unknown selection names the file and points to examples.**
  - `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` checks the unknown `DEFAULT` name and the missing-configuration case. It looks for the file path and `editing-the-file`.
  - `configurations_without_any_selection_report_how_to_choose_one` covers the case where no selection exists.
  - `unknown_selections_name_the_file_that_made_them` checks which file is named for a dangling user default, project selection, workspace default and `--config`. It also checks that the absence of a workspace file is reflected.
- **Bedrock explicit profile and region.**
  - `omitted_bedrock_profile_and_region_use_standard_sdk_resolution` compares the omitted case with the standard SDK loader. It checks that an explicit profile matches the standard loader with that profile. It also checks that an explicit region overrides the profile's region.
  - `explicit_bedrock_credentials_reach_the_sdk_without_the_default_chain` covers an explicit region.
  - `bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools` checks at the CLI that the profile's credentials and the explicit region `us-west-2` are used instead of the default credentials.
  - `all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections` checks that, with neither set, the SDK default chain's credentials and region (`ap-south-1`) are used.
- **Ollama default endpoint.** `backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults` asserts `endpoint()` is `http://localhost:11434`. A configured endpoint is exercised in every CLI test.
- **`api_key_env`.** `ollama_authentication_resolves_separately_and_rejects_missing_values` covers a missing variable, an empty variable and a present variable. `missing_or_empty_api_key_env_fails_before_any_model_request` runs the CLI for ollama and openai with the variable unset and empty. It asserts failure, that stderr names the variable, that the listener was never contacted, and that the evidence file is unchanged. `openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage` checks that the configured variable's value is sent as the bearer credential.
- **OpenAI defaults.**
  - `openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials` asserts the default endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
  - The same test asserts that `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the variable resolved when neither `api_key` nor `api_key_env` is set, and that the call fails when it is absent.
  - The same test checks that a custom `api_key_env` is resolved by name.
  - `all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections` confirms this end to end with `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

I found no obligation or named failure case without a test that asserts its outcome. All tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.
